rules.text: Every player must obey the rules in force at the moment a move is submitted. Each rule is either immutable or mutable, and carries a number that is never reused.
The rulebook changes only through a proposal that has been voted on and accepted. Nothing else alters the text of a rule.
A move is judged against the rulebook version and hash that were fixed before the move was submitted. A rule enacted later never applies to a move that has already been judged.
A mutable rule may be amended or repealed. An immutable rule may be neither, until an accepted proposal has first transmuted it into a mutable rule.
If the rulebook reaches a state the contract cannot execute, the game ends immediately and the player whose accepted proposal produced that state wins.
Players take turns in the order they joined. A turn is one move that was judged legal, or one proposal that has been resolved.
On your turn you may claim points by declaring a whole number of points from 1 to 6. A claim outside that range is not legal.
A player who holds 100 points or more wins, once that player has claimed the win and the claim has been judged legal.
A proposal is accepted when the votes in its favour are at least 60 percent of the votes cast, and at least half the players have voted.
At most 16 rules may be in force at once. While the rulebook is full, a proposal to enact a further rule is not legal.

changes.after: Ten starting rules: 101 to 105 immutable, 201 to 205 mutable.
